# Lectio (enjoyhim.org)

> Lectio is a bilingual (English / Chinese) web app for the daily Christian
> practice of Lectio Divina — "divine reading." Each day it guides a reader
> through a short lectionary scripture passage in four movements: Lectio
> (reading), Meditatio (reflection), Oratio (response), and Contemplatio
> (rest), and reads the passage aloud. It also offers a library of 101 Bible
> verses for reflection and an assistant that answers questions about
> scripture and the practice.

Lectio Divina is an ancient Christian prayer practice: a short passage is read
slowly, reflected on, responded to in prayer, and then sat with in silence.
Lectio (the app) never predicts the future and does not offer fortune-telling;
its focus is on meeting the reader's real questions with scripture and gentle
reflection.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://enjoyhim.org/): start today's reading; a question-led
  daily scripture reflection.
- [Today](https://enjoyhim.org/today): walk the church calendar's passage
  for today, one step at a time (Lectio, Meditatio, Oratio, Contemplatio),
  with audio narration.
- [Verse Library](https://enjoyhim.org/library): 101 Bible verses with
  bilingual text and reflection themes. Each verse has its own page, e.g.
  [Psalm 23:1](https://enjoyhim.org/library/psalm-23-1).
- [Approach](https://enjoyhim.org/approach): what Lectio Divina is, what
  it is not, and how this app practices it.
- [Pricing](https://enjoyhim.org/pricing): guests get 3 Daily Word readings
  a day, free accounts 6 a day plus trial credits (Lectio Divina ×3, Deep
  Lectio ×1); Basic $4.99/mo (Daily Word and Lectio Divina layouts), Pro
  $11.99/mo (all layouts, unlimited). First month free on monthly plans;
  annual billing saves 40%.

## How it works

- Readings are drawn from the Revised Common Lectionary; each calendar day has
  one passage, the same for every reader.
- The passage can be listened to (audio narration in English and Chinese).
- Readers may keep a private journal of reflections (requires a free account);
  journals are never shared or published.
- The site is fully bilingual: every page is available in English and Chinese
  via the language links or `?lang=en` / `?lang=zh`.

## For AI crawlers

Content pages (home, today, library, approach, pricing, privacy) may be
indexed and quoted. Private reader pages (/login, /account, /history) and all
/api/ endpoints must not be crawled. A machine-readable sitemap is at
https://enjoyhim.org/sitemap.xml.

## Sources & further reading

- lectio-divina.org — fifty years of monastic reflections on Scripture and
  the Fathers (Hebrew Scriptures, New Testament, the early Church,
  patristics: Origen, Gregory of Nyssa, Bernard of Clairvaux), including a
  rich essay on the etymology and meaning of lectio divina itself. The
  "roots of the practice" section on /approach draws on it.
